```{r setup, include=FALSE}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.align='center', echo = FALSE)

# load packages
suppressWarnings(suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(knitr)
  library(reshape2)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(gridExtra)
  library(scales)
  library(tidyr)
  library(forcats)
  library(ComplexUpset)
  library(plyr)
  library(vioplot)
  library(corrplot)
  library(cowplot)
  library(kableExtra)
  library(tibble)
  library(ChIPQC)
  library(plotly)
  library(pheatmap)
}))

options(scipen=5)

## load config variables
source(params$configFile)

col_vals_pass  <- c(
  "FALSE" = "#D55E00",  # vermillion (fail)
  "TRUE"  = "#009E73"   # bluish green (pass)
)

```

This report provides a summary of the first stage of PIPPA QC pipeline. It confirms the success of an ATAC-seq experiment from the resulting sequencing data. It looks at metrics from the raw sequencing data, alignment, filtering, peak calling and ATAC-seq-specific quality metrics. The bioinformatics pipeline parallels that of the [ENCODE ATAC-seq guidelines](https://www.encodeproject.org/atac-seq/). Raw fastq files have been have been aligned with Bowtie2 to the human genome (hg38) and peaks called with MACS3 for each individual sample. Thresholds applied for pass/failed samples should be specified in the config.r file.

```{r loadDat, message = FALSE, results='hide'}
## import data
pheno<-read.csv(sampleSheet, header = TRUE, sep = ',', stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
pheno$sequencingBatch <- as.factor(pheno$sequencingBatch)
processSum <- read.csv(processSumFile, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, strip.white = TRUE)
fastqc<-read.table(fastqcFile, sep = "\t", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
readCounts<-read.table(readCountsFile, fill = TRUE, skip = 1)
alignQC<-read.table(alignmentFile, sep = "\t", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# wrangle data
missingCol<-setdiff(c("sequencingBatch", "sampleID", "sampleCode", "cohort", "fraction", "experiment", "individualID"), colnames(pheno))
if (length(missingCol) != 0 ) {
  if ("sequencingBatch" %in% missingCol){
    pheno$sequencingBatch<-pheno$cohort
      if (length(missingCol) > 1) {
      warning('Incorrect column names. Missing column(s): ', list(missingCol))
      stop()
    }
  }
}
## exclude duplicates from metadata
dups<-names(which(table(paste(pheno$individualID, pheno$fraction, pheno$tissue, sep = "_")) > 1))
pheno<-unique(pheno[,intersect(c("sequencingBatch", "sampleID","sampleCode", "cohort","fraction","individualID", "tissue"), colnames(pheno))])

```

Metadata includes information about `r nrow(pheno)` samples from `r length(unique(pheno$individualID))` individuals. Results for `r nrow(processSum)` samples that have been processed in the Stage 1 of QC are shown in this report.

```{r}
idx <- match(pheno$sampleID, processSum$sampleID)
processSum <- processSum[idx[!is.na(idx)], ]
processSum$sampleCode <- pheno[match(processSum$sampleID, pheno$sampleID),]$sampleCode
colsKeep<-c("sampleID","sampleCode", "R1Filename","R2Filename")
mergeStats <- processSum[,colsKeep]

## wrangle multiqc stats to retain important columns
colsKeep<-c("Total.Sequences","total_deduplicated_percentage", "Sequences.flagged.as.poor.quality")
R1stats <- fastqc[match(processSum$R1Filename, fastqc$Filename),colsKeep]
colnames(R1stats) <- paste0(colnames(R1stats) , "_R1")
R2stats <- fastqc[match(processSum$R2Filename, fastqc$Filename),colsKeep]
colnames(R2stats) <- paste0(colnames(R2stats) , "_R2")
mergeStats<-cbind(mergeStats,R1stats,R2stats )

## calculate percentage of mitochondrial reads
readCounts<-readCounts[match(mergeStats$sampleID, readCounts$V1),]
MTpercentReads <- readCounts$V2/readCounts$V3*100
mergeStats$"PercentMTReads" <- MTpercentReads

## select alignment columns and match to sampleIDs
aIndex<-match(mergeStats$sampleID, gsub("\\.bowtie", "", alignQC$Sample))
alignQC$aligned_total<-rowSums(alignQC[,c("paired_aligned_one", "paired_aligned_multi")])
mergeStats<-cbind(mergeStats,alignQC[aIndex,c("overall_alignment_rate", "aligned_total")])

## load flagstat metrics calculated as part of encode qc pipeline
files<-list.files(paste0(alignedDir, "/ENCODEMetrics"), pattern = "\\.pbc\\.qc$")
eMetrics <- do.call(rbind, lapply(files, function(each) {
  tmp <- read.table(
    file.path(alignedDir, "ENCODEMetrics", each)
  )
  if (ncol(tmp) != 7) {
    tmp <- as.data.frame(matrix(NA, nrow = 1, ncol = 7))
  }
  tmp$sampleID <- sub("\\.pbc\\.qc$", "", each)
  tmp
}))

colnames(eMetrics)<-c("TotalReadPairs_afterAlignment","DistinctReadPairs","OneReadPair","TwoReadPairs","NRF","PBC1","PBC2", "Sample")
eIndex<-match(mergeStats$sampleID, eMetrics$Sample)
eMetrics<-eMetrics[eIndex,]
mergeStats<-cbind(mergeStats,eMetrics)
mergeStats <- subset(mergeStats, select = -Sample)

## Merge Peak calling and FRIP results
fripStats <- read.csv(file.path(fripFile), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, strip.white = TRUE)
fripStats$FripMACS3PE <- fripStats$ReadsinBAMPeaks/fripStats$BAMTotalReads
eIndex<-match(mergeStats$sampleID, fripStats$SampleName)
fripStats<-fripStats[eIndex,]
mergeStats <- cbind(mergeStats, fripStats[, c("ReadsinBAMPeaks","BAMTotalReads","BAMPeaks","FripMACS3PE")] )

## load periodicity metrics 
filePaths <- list.files(file.path(alignedDir,"/QCOutput/"), pattern = "FragmentDistribution_*")
propNucleosomesAll <- do.call(rbind, lapply(filePaths, function(each) {

  load(file.path(alignedDir, "QCOutput", each))

  propNucleosomes
}))
colnames(propNucleosomesAll) <- c("NFR", "Mono", "Di", "Tri", "Quad")
eIndex<-match(mergeStats$sampleID, rownames(propNucleosomesAll))
propNucleosomesAll<-propNucleosomesAll[eIndex,]
mergeStats <- cbind(mergeStats,propNucleosomesAll)
                    
diptestStatsAll <- do.call(rbind, lapply(filePaths, function(each) {

  load(file.path(alignedDir, "QCOutput", each))

  diptestStats
}))
eIndex<-match(mergeStats$sampleID, gsub("\\.D$", "", rownames(diptestStatsAll)))
diptestStatsAll<-diptestStatsAll[eIndex,]
mergeStats <- cbind(mergeStats,diptestStatsAll)

## add more metadata info
mergeStats <- mergeStats %>%
  left_join(pheno %>% select("sampleID","sequencingBatch","cohort", "fraction"), by = "sampleID")

## count number of samples with X million reads
readThres<-seq(0,max(mergeStats$Total.Sequences_R1, na.rm = TRUE)+10^6, 10^6)
nSamples<-matrix(data = NA, nrow = length(readThres), ncol = length(unique(mergeStats$sequencingBatch))+1)
for(i in readThres){
  nSamples[1+(i/10^6),1] <- sum(mergeStats$Total.Sequences_R1 > i, na.rm = TRUE)
  colNum<-2
  for(each in unique(mergeStats$sequencingBatch)){
    nSamples[1+(i/10^6),colNum] <- sum(mergeStats[which(mergeStats$sequencingBatch == each),3] > i, na.rm = TRUE)
    colNum<-colNum+1
  }
}

## a successful ATAC experiment should have decreasing proportions in the nucleosome, mono, di,tri- nucleosomes
## define a tolerance for these comparisons
tol <- 0
decreasingProps<-cbind(mergeStats$NFR+tol > mergeStats$Mono, 
                       mergeStats$Mono+tol > mergeStats$Di, 
                       mergeStats$Di+tol > mergeStats$Tri
)
colnames(decreasingProps)<-c("NFR>Mono", "Mono>Di", "Di>Tri")
mergeStats <- cbind(mergeStats,decreasingProps)

## Load TSS enrichment scores
tssSamples <- read.table(tssEnrich,header= TRUE)
eIndex<-match(mergeStats$sampleID, tssSamples$sample)
tssSamples<-tssSamples[eIndex,]
mergeStats <- cbind(mergeStats,TSSScore = tssSamples$"TSS_enrichment")

mergeStats$Ratio <- mergeStats$NFR/mergeStats$Mono
mergeStats$overall_alignment_rate[is.na(mergeStats$overall_alignment_rate)] <- 0
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
kbl(nCTStart) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"),font_size = 10)

```

## 1. Sequencing

### 1.1 Data summary

In total there were `r signif(sum(c(mergeStats$Total.Sequences_R1, mergeStats$Total.Sequences_R2), na.rm = TRUE)/1000000,3)` million reads generated across all samples, with a mean of 
`r signif(mean(c(mergeStats$Total.Sequences_R1, mergeStats$Total.Sequences_R2), na.rm = TRUE)/1000000,3)` million per sample (SD = `r signif(sd(c(mergeStats$Total.Sequences_R1, mergeStats$Total.Sequences_R2), na.rm = TRUE)/1000000,3)` million). 

The median number of reads was  `r signif(median(c(mergeStats$Total.Sequences_R1, mergeStats$Total.Sequences_R2), na.rm = TRUE)/1000000,3)` million per sample (IQR = `r signif(sd(c(mergeStats$Total.Sequences_R1, mergeStats$Total.Sequences_R2), na.rm = TRUE)/1000000,3)` million).

The plots below summarise the distributions of the raw sequencing data for `r sum(!is.na(mergeStats$Total.Sequences_R1)) ` samples. For mammalian studies, authors of the ATAC-seq protocol recommend a minimum of 50 million non-duplicated, non-mitochondrial mapped reads for open chromatin detection. The ENCODE pipeline recommends a minimum of 25 million for single end and 50 million for paired. In the plots below, the median of the data is indicated by the orange line and 50 and 25 million thresholds by the black lines. The red lines indicates the threshold that has been applied by the user (specified in the config.r file).

```{r pressure, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 10}
# plot histograms of read numbers and % unique reads
xlab <- c('Number of Reads', '% unique reads' , 'Number of Reads', '% unique reads')
cols2Plot <- c("Total.Sequences_R1", "total_deduplicated_percentage_R1", "Total.Sequences_R2","total_deduplicated_percentage_R2")
read<-c('R1','R1','R2', 'R2')
p=NULL
for (x in 1:4){
  p[[x]]<-mergeStats %>% dplyr::select(all_of(cols2Plot))%>%
          ggplot(aes(x = .[,1]))+ # select x values based on column index rather than name
          geom_histogram(bins = 100,fill ='gray')+
          labs(title = read[x], x = xlab[x], y = 'Number of Samples')+
          theme_bw() #+
#	scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = "M", scale = 1e-6))
}

## add thresholds
p[[1]]<-p[[1]]+ geom_vline(xintercept = median(mergeStats$Total.Sequences_R1, na.rm = TRUE), color = "orange") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(25000000,50000000), color = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = numReads*10^6, color = "red")+
	scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = "M", scale = 1e-6))
p[[3]]<-p[[3]]+ geom_vline(xintercept = median(mergeStats$Total.Sequences_R2, na.rm = TRUE), color = "orange") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(25000000,50000000), color = "black")+
  geom_vline(xintercept = numReads*10^6, color = "red")+
	scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = "M", scale = 1e-6))

grid.arrange(grobs = p,ncol=2)
```

A good ATAC-seq experiment will capture enrichment at a broad range of genomic locations. The number of distinct or unique reads is an indicator of the diversity or complexity of the data. If the sample does not contain sufficient DNA and/or has been over-sequenced, you will simply be repeatedly sequencing PCR duplicates of a restricted pool of distinct DNA fragments. This is known a low-complexity library and is not desirable.  

``` {r uniqueReads}

  geom_point() +
  labs(x = 'Number of Reads (R1)', y = '% unique reads (R1)', label = "Sample ID", colour = "Cell-fraction")+
  scale_color_manual(values = colorBlindGrey8[1:length(unique(mergeStats$fraction))])+
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = 'bottom')

p[[2]] <- ggplot(mergeStats, aes(x =  Total.Sequences_R2, y = total_deduplicated_percentage_R2, colour = fraction, label= sampleCode))+
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = 'Number of Reads (R2)', y = '% unique reads (R2)', label = "Sample ID", colour = "Cell-fraction")+
  scale_color_manual(values = colorBlindGrey8[1:length(unique(mergeStats$fraction))])+
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = 'right')

ggplotly(p[[1]],tooltip = "label")
```

## 2. Alignment


### 2.1 Summary of alignment (pre-filtering)

The plot below shows the alignment rate and number of mapped reads per sample. While general convention is a unique mapping rate over 80% is typical for a successful ATAC-seq experiment, ENCODE would require that the percentage of mapped reads should be greater than 95%, though values >80% may be acceptable. In the plot below the pink line indicates the 80% threshold, the black indicates the 95%. The plot below contains data for `r sum(!is.na(mergeStats$aligned_total))` samples. Threshold chosen by user is indicated as a red line.

```{r alignment rate}
## plot alignment rate against number of reads
p <-ggplot(mergeStats, aes(x = aligned_total, y = overall_alignment_rate, colour = fraction, label = sampleCode))+
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept=c(95, 80, alignThres), #acceptable
             color = c('black', colorBlindGrey8[2], "red"))+
  labs(x = 'Number of Reads Pairs', y = 'Alignment rate (%)',colour = "Cell-fraction")+
  theme_bw() +
  scale_color_manual(values = colorBlindGrey8[1:length(unique(mergeStats$fraction))])+
  theme(legend.position = 'bottom')+
	scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = "M", scale = 1e-6))
ggplotly(p, tooltip = "label")
```



### 2.2 Mitochondrial genome

It can be a useful QC to assess the number of mitochondrial reads; some ATAC-Seq samples have been reported to be 80% mitochondrial reads. 

``` {r mitochondria, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 10}

for (i in 1:length(colsCol)) {
    df <- data.frame(x = mergeStats[[colsCol[i]]],y = mergeStats$PercentMTReads)
    p[[i]] <- ggplot(df,aes(x=x, y=y, fill = x))+

      axis.text = element_text(size = 12),

    )

grid.arrange(grobs = p, nrow = 3)
```

### 2.3 Library Complexity

In this section we will assess the number of unique aligned read pairs as the number of total reads pairs increases, across all samples. 

``` {r dedupreads}
# plot unique reads against total reads
p <- ggplot(mergeStats,aes(x=TotalReadPairs_afterAlignment, y = DistinctReadPairs, colour = factor(fraction),label = sampleCode))+
      geom_point()+
      theme_bw()+
      labs(x = "Number of read pairs", y = "Number of distinct read pairs",colour = "Cell-fraction")+
      scale_color_manual(values = colorBlindGrey8[1:length(unique(mergeStats$fraction))])+
      theme(legend.title = element_blank(), 
            legend.position = 'bottom') +
	scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = "M", scale = 1e-6))+
	scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = "M", scale = 1e-6))
ggplotly(p, tooltip = "label")
```

We will also calculate additional statistics recommended by the ENCODE ATAC-seq pipeline: PCR Bottlenecking Coefficients 1 & 2 (PBC1 & PBC2) and Non-Redundant Fraction (NRF) and compare these to their reference values. The plots below contain data from `r sum(!is.na(eMetrics[,1]))` samples.

``` {r encode, fig.height = 10}
## plot encode statistics
p <- list()
## to ensure the threshold labels are in correct place according to threshold lines, calculate midpoints between lines:
# matrix of encode thresholds
thres<-matrix(c(nrfThres, 0.9,
               nrfThres, 0.9, 
               1, 3), nrow = 2)
# matrix of label orientation (mean)
labs<-matrix(data=NA, ncol = 3, nrow = 3)
labs[2, ]<-colMeans(thres)
labsText<-list(c("Concerning", "Acceptable", "Ideal"), c("Severe", "Concerning", "None"), c("Severe", "Concerning", "None"))

for (x in 1:3){
  colNum<-x+4 # index to correct column according to label
  min<-min(eMetrics[,colNum], na.rm = TRUE)
  max<-max(eMetrics[,colNum], na.rm = TRUE)
  # generate the placement of the labels relative to the data
  if (min < thres[1, x]){
    labs[1, x]<-mean(c(min, thres[1, x]))
  } else { labs[1, x]<-thres[1, x]-sd(eMetrics[,colNum], na.rm = TRUE) } 
  if(max > thres[2, x]){
    labs[3, x]<-mean(c(max, thres[2, x]))
  } else { labs[3, x]<- thres[2, x]+sd(eMetrics[,colNum], na.rm = TRUE) }
  
  # create plot
  p[[x]]<-dplyr::select(eMetrics, all_of(colNum)) %>%
    ggplot(aes_string(x=names(.)[1]))+
    geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill ='white', colour = 'black')+
    labs(y = "Number of samples")+
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(thres[,x]))+
    annotate("text", x = labs[,x], y = Inf, vjust = 2, label = labsText[[x]])+
    theme_bw()+
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 90))
  
}
grid.arrange(grobs = p, nrow = 3)

```

``` {r encode2, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 12}
      )
    x <- x + 1
  }
}
grid.arrange(grobs = p,ncol=3)
```

### 2.4 Fragment Size Distribution

ATAC-seq data should be enriched for specific sized fragments, so the distribution of fragment size should show periodicity. Typically there should be a large proportion of reads with fragment length < 100bp indicating nucleosome-free fragments, the plot should then show periodicity of ~ 200bp representing  enrichment of mono-, di-, and tri-nucleosome bound fragments (~200, 400, 600bp, respectively). Typically we would look at the fragment distribution where a successful ATAC-seq experiment would have a peak at ~50-100bp with a large proportion of reads less than 100 bp, and peaks at 200bp, 400bp, 600bp. If there was no chromatin in the sample the graph would have no periodicity and resemble a poisson distribution with lambda = 1). Instead to make this tractable across hundred of samples we have classified the fragments into bins representing nucleosome-free,mono-, di-, tri, and quad-nucleosome bound fragments. From this for each sample we can calculate the proportion within in each bin and apply filters/conditions. If in general the ATAC-seq has worked, we would expect to see decreasing proportions across the violins below. The plot below contains data from `r sum(!is.na(propNucleosomesAll[,1]))` samples.  

``` {r periodicity}
## plot nucleosome periodicity
melt(na.omit(propNucleosomesAll)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=as.factor(Var2), y=value))+
      geom_violin(fill = "grey80", scale = 'width')+
      geom_boxplot(width=0.05, fill='black')+
      labs(y = "Proportion of reads", x = "Nucleosome")+
      stat_summary(fun="median", geom="point", color="white")+
      scale_x_discrete(labels = c("NFR", "Mono", "Di", "Tri", "Quad"))+
      theme_bw()
```

``` {r  fig.width = 10, fig.height = 12}
## plot nucleosome periodicity
propNucleosomesAll.1 <- mergeStats[, c("fraction", "sequencingBatch","cohort","NFR", "Mono", "Di", "Tri", "Quad")]
melt.df  <- propNucleosomesAll.1 %>%
pivot_longer(
    cols = 4:8,                     # first 4 columns
    names_to = "FragSize",     # new column for fragment names
    values_to = "percentage"        # new column for values
  )
melt.df <- as.data.frame(melt.df)
melt.df <- melt.df %>%
  mutate(FragSize = fct_reorder(FragSize, percentage)) %>%
  mutate(FragSize = factor(FragSize, levels=c("NFR", "Mono", "Di", "Tri", "Quad")))

p <- list()
colsCol <- c("fraction", "sequencingBatch","cohort")
labsCol <- c("Cell-fraction", "Sequencing batch", "Brain bank")
for (i in 1:length(colsCol)) {
    p[[i]] <- ggplot(melt.df,aes(x=as.factor(FragSize), y=percentage, fill = .data[[colsCol[i]]]))+
      geom_violin(scale = "width",
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
            trim = FALSE) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.15,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
               outlier.shape = NA)+
      labs(y = "Proportion of reads", x = "Fragment size classification", fill = labsCol[i])+
       scale_fill_manual(values = colorBlindGrey8[1:length(unique(melt.df[[colsCol[i]]]))])+
     theme_bw() +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16)
    )
}


grid.arrange(grobs = p,ncol=1)
```    
      
We need to apply thresholds to satisfy the following criteria

* large proportion of nucleosome-free fragments
* presence of mono-nucleosome bound fragments
* decreasing number of fragments in fragment bins.

```{r periodicity2}

# plot proportion of nucleosome free against mono
p <-ggplot(mergeStats, aes(x=Mono, y=NFR, color = factor(fraction)))+
    geom_point()+
    theme_bw()+
    labs(x= "Proportion fragments classed as mono", y = "Proportion fragments class as nucleosome free", 
         color = "Cell-fraction")+
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1)+
  scale_color_manual(values = rep(colorBlindGrey8,
               ceiling(length(unique(mergeStats$fraction)) / length(colorBlindGrey8)))[1:length(unique(mergeStats$fraction))])+
    ylim(c(0,1))+
    xlim(c(0,max(propNucleosomesAll[,2])))+
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(nucfThres))+
  
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(monoThres)) + 
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16)
  )


p
```

Alternatively we can test for periodicity (i.e. multimodality) using Hartigan's Dip test for Unimodality. Here a significant p-value indicates the presence of multiple modes as we would expect in a successful ATAC experiment. The plot below contains data from `r sum(!is.na(diptestStatsAll[,1]))` samples.  


```{r periodicity3}

# plot distribution of hartigan's dip test p values
hist(mergeStats[,"p.value"], breaks = 50, col = "grey", xlab = "Hartigans Test P-value", ylab = "Number of samples", main = "")
abline(v = dipPThres)


p<- ggplot(mergeStats, aes(x = p.value, fill = fraction))+
  geom_histogram(bins = 100)+    facet_wrap(~fraction, scales = "free")+  
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = dipPThres), colour = "black",
             linetype = "dashed") + 
  theme_bw()+
  labs(x =  "Hartigans Test P-value", y = "Number of samples", 
       fill = "cell-fraction",title = "")+
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")+
  scale_fill_manual(values = colorBlindGrey8[1:length(unique(melt.df[[colsCol[i]]]))])

p
```


## 3. Peak calling

### 3.1 Number of peaks

Peak calling was performed using MACS3 in the paired end and narrow peak mode. ENCODE recommends that number of peaks in each sample be greater than 150,000, though values greater than 100,000 are acceptable. Data from `r sum(!is.na(mergeStats$BAMPeaks))` samples is plotted below. The mean number of peaks for MACS3 PE Peaks is `r signif(mean(mergeStats$BAMPeaks, na.rm = TRUE ),3)` (SD = `r signif(sd(mergeStats$BAMPeaks, na.rm = TRUE ),3)`). The plots below contain data from `r sum(!is.na(mergeStats$BAMPeaks))` samples. 

```{r numpeaks, results=FALSE}
p <-ggplot(mergeStats, aes(x = BAMTotalReads, y =  BAMPeaks, colour = fraction, label = sampleCode))+
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = 'Number of Reads (after alignment QC)', y = 'Number of peaks ',colour = "Cell-fraction")+
  theme_bw() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(150000, 100000), color = c('black', colorBlindGrey8[3]))+
  scale_color_manual(values = colorBlindGrey8[1:length(unique(mergeStats$fraction))])+
  theme(legend.position = 'bottom')+
	scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = "M", scale = 1e-6))
ggplotly(p, tooltip = "label")

```

### 3.2 Specificity of reads in peaks

Plot of the fraction of reads in peaks called for that sample. These plots give a good indication of how "enriched" the sample is and can be considered a "signal-to-noise" measure of what proportion of the library consists of fragments from binding sites vs. background reads. According to the ENCODE standard processing pipeline for ATAC-seq the FRiP score should be > 0.3, though values greater than 0.2 are acceptable. We will not filter on this metric yet, but return to it once we have called peaks at the group level. 

```{r readsinpeaks}
p<- ggplot(mergeStats, aes(x=BAMPeaks, y = FripMACS3PE, colour = fraction, label = sampleCode))+
    geom_point()+
    theme_bw()+
    labs( x = "Number of peaks (100000s)", y = "Fraction reads in peaks", label = "sampleCode", color = "Cell-fraction")+
    scale_color_manual(values = colorBlindGrey8[1:length(unique(mergeStats$fraction))])+
    scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = "", scale = 1e-5))+
    theme(legend.title = element_blank(), 
          legend.position = 'bottom')
ggplotly(p, tooltip ="label")
```

# QC Summary: Sample Filtering

```{r samplePASS}
# generate a txt file of passed samples
QCPASS<-cbind(mergeStats$overall_alignment_rate > alignThres, #alignment rate 
              mergeStats$BAMTotalReads > numReads*10^6,#total filtered & aligned reads
              mergeStats$NRF > nrfThres, #encode
              mergeStats$PBC1 > pbc1Thres, #encode
              mergeStats$PBC2 > pbc2Thres, #encode,
              mergeStats$NFR > nucfThres, #fractions nucleosome free 
              mergeStats$Mono > monoThres
              ) 
QCPASS[is.na(QCPASS)] <- FALSE
colnames(QCPASS)<-c("AlignmentRate", "TotalNumReads", "NRF", "PBC1", "PBC2","NFR", "MNC")
keep<-rowSums(QCPASS) == ncol(QCPASS)
QCPASS.df<-cbind(QCPASS, "QCPASS" = keep)
QCPASS.df <- cbind(mergeStats[,c("sampleID","sampleCode","fraction","cohort","sequencingBatch")],QCPASS.df)
write.csv(QCPASS.df, file = file.path(qc1pass))

write.table(mergeStats$sampleID[keep], file = file.path(qc1passList), 
            row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)

qcStats <- cbind(mergeStats[,c("sampleID","sampleCode","cohort","fraction","sequencingBatch")],mergeStats$overall_alignment_rate, #alignment rate 
              mergeStats$BAMTotalReads, #total filtered & aligned reads
              mergeStats$NRF, #encode
              mergeStats$PBC1, #encode
              mergeStats$PBC2, #encode,
              mergeStats$NFR, #fractions nucleosome free 
              mergeStats$Mono, #fractions mononucleosome 
              mergeStats[["NFR>Mono"]],#periodicity
              mergeStats$BAMPeaks, # number of peaks
              mergeStats$FripMACS3PE, #frip
              mergeStats[["p.value"]],mergeStats$TSSScore
                     #multimodality
              ) 

colnames(qcStats) <- c("sampleID","sampleCode","cohort","fraction","sequencingBatch", "AlignmentRate", "TotalNumReads", "NRF", "PBC1", "PBC2","NFR", "MNC", "Periodicity","Peaks", "FRIP", "Multimodality", "TSS_score")
write.csv(qcStats, file = file.path(qc1stats),row.names = FALSE)
```

Samples will now be filtered based on thresholds defined in the config file. The table below, summarises the number of samples that pass each QC step.

```{r}
kbl(colSums(QCPASS, na.rm = TRUE))
```

The table below, summarises the number of samples that fail each QC step.
```{r, echo = FALSE}
QCPASS.df2 <- QCPASS.df[,c("AlignmentRate", "TotalNumReads", "NRF", "PBC1", "PBC2","NFR", "MNC", "QCPASS")]

# create cross tab table
xTab<-matrix(data = NA, ncol = ncol(QCPASS.df2), nrow = ncol(QCPASS.df2))
for(i in 1:ncol(QCPASS.df2)){
  for(j in 1:ncol(QCPASS.df2)){
    xTab[i,j]<-sum(rowSums(QCPASS.df2[,c(i,j)]) == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
}
colnames(xTab)<-colnames(QCPASS.df2)
rownames(xTab)<-colnames(QCPASS.df2)

kbl(xTab) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

```

## Correlations between QC metrics

This is a correlation matrix of the QC metrics considered so far which enables us to see whether lower quality samples fail across multiple metrics. 

``` {r correlation, fig.width = 10, fig.height= 10}
## create correlation plot 
cols2Keep <- c("TSSScore","BAMTotalReads", "TotalReadPairs_afterAlignment","total_deduplicated_percentage_R1","Sequences.flagged.as.poor.quality_R1",
               "PercentMTReads","overall_alignment_rate", "DistinctReadPairs","NRF","PBC1","PBC2", "NFR", "MNC","p.value",
               "BAMPeaks","FripMACS3PE")
corMergeStats<-mergeStats[,cols2Keep]
colnames(corMergeStats)<- c("tss",'total\nreads', 'total\npairs','dedup', 'poor\nqual', 'mt\nreads', 'alignt\nrate', 'distinct\nreads', 
                            'NFR','PBC1',  "PBC2","PropNFR", "PropMNC", "DipP","NPeaks_PE", "FRIP_PE")
corMergeStats<- corMergeStats[, colSums(corMergeStats, na.rm = TRUE) != 0]
corrplot.mixed(cor(corMergeStats, use = "p"), order = 'AOE', tl.cex=0.7, tl.col = 'black')
```

Below there is a summary of the QC metrics that samples failed the most and the most common combinations of failed QC metrics.

```{r fig.width = 12, fig.height= 10}

qc_cols <- names(QCPASS.df2)
qc_cols <- qc_cols[!qc_cols == "QCPASS"]

fail_long <- QCPASS.df2 %>%
  mutate(sample_id = row_number()) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(qc_cols),
               names_to = "metric",
               values_to = "pass") %>%
  filter(!pass) %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  summarise(fail_combo = paste(metric, collapse = ";"), .groups = "drop")

combo_rank <- fail_long %>%
  dplyr::count(fail_combo, sort = TRUE)%>%
  slice_max(n, n = 20)

p <- list()
p[[1]] <-  ggplot(combo_rank,aes(x = reorder(fail_combo, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = "Failed QC combination",
    y = "Number of samples"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

fail_counts <- QCPASS.df2 %>%
  dplyr::mutate(n_fail = rowSums(!across(all_of(qc_cols)))) %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_fail > 0) %>%
  dplyr::count(n_fail)

p[[2]]  <- ggplot(fail_counts, aes(n_fail, n)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(fail_counts$n_fail))) +
  labs(
    x = "QC metrics failed",
    y = "Samples"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

grid.arrange(grobs = p, ncol=2)
```

```{r}
qc_cols_use <- qc_cols[
  colSums(QCPASS.df2[qc_cols]) > 0 &      # not all FALSE
  colSums(!QCPASS.df2[qc_cols]) > 0       # not all TRUE
]

qc_fail <- QCPASS.df2[qc_cols_use] == FALSE
qc_fail <- qc_fail[rowSums(qc_fail) > 0, ]

ComplexUpset::upset(
  as.data.frame(qc_fail),
  intersect = colnames(qc_fail),
  name = "QC failures"
)
```
